PREVIOUS EXPLORATION:

Hypothesis: Patients with elevated lactate dehydrogenase activity—as approximated by high LDHA gene expression—exhibit higher tumor proliferation (mitotic count) and a distinct proliferation‐related gene expression signature compared to patients with low LDHA expression.

Experiment objective: Because clinical LDH annotations are too sparse, use LDHA gene expression as a continuous proxy for LDH activity. Test whether high LDHA expression correlates with increased mitotic counts and distinct differential expression of proliferation genes.

Steps for the programmer:
1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_gene_expression.csv (genes × samples); ensure sample barcodes match first 12 characters to clinical bcr_patient_barcode.  
2. From gene expression data, extract the row corresponding to LDHA (HUGO symbol: “LDHA”) and compute its expression per sample.  
3. Map each sample’s LDHA expression to its patient record; merge with clinical data.  
4. Filter to patients with non‐missing mitotic_count_per_mm2 and age_at_diagnosis and gender.  
5. Dichotomize patients into “High‐LDHA” vs “Low‐LDHA” groups around the median LDHA expression.  
6. Compare mitotic_count_per_mm2 between High vs Low LDHA groups using an appropriate two‐sample test (t‐test or Wilcoxon).  
7. Build a linear model (e.g., OLS) or use limma to identify genes differentially expressed between High‐LDHA vs Low‐LDHA, adjusting for age_at_diagnosis and gender. Apply FDR correction and extract genes with FDR<0.05.  
8. From a curated proliferation gene set (e.g., Hallmark E2F targets), test for enrichment among genes upregulated in the High‐LDHA group via Fisher’s exact test or preranked GSEA.  
9. Visualize results: volcano plot for DE genes and a bar or dot plot of enrichment statistics.

Deliverables:
• Table of patient counts, group means, test statistics, and p‐value for mitotic count comparison.  
• Data frame of DE results: gene, logFC, p‐value, FDR.  
• Volcano plot of differential expression (highlighting FDR<0.05).  
• Enrichment analysis report: overlap counts, odds ratio, p‐value for proliferation gene set.  
• Brief summary PDF or notebook section interpreting whether high LDHA expression is associated with increased mitotic count and proliferation signature.

Analysis:
The analysis completed successfully with 170 samples (85 High‐LDHA, 85 Low‐LDHA):

• Mitotic count comparison (High vs Low LDHA): t = 0.412, p = 0.681 → no significant difference.  
• Differential expression (OLS adjusting for age and gender): 17,519 genes at FDR < 0.05.  
• Top 10 DE genes (sorted by FDR):
  – ENSG00000134333.13: logFC=+1.26, FDR=5.96e-33
  – ENSG00000166788.9: logFC=+0.69, FDR=9.61e-08
  – ENSG00000181444.12: logFC=–1.25, FDR=1.02e-07
  – …

Volcano plot shows many significant genes (red) at both positive and negative log‐fold changes. Enrichment for E2F targets was not performed (requires gene set library).

Review:
The revised experiment substituted LDHA expression for sparse clinical LDH measurements, following the updated plan. It successfully dichotomized 170 patients into High/Low LDHA groups, performed a t-test on mitotic counts (no significant difference: p=0.681), and conducted gene-wise OLS (adjusting for age and gender) identifying 17,519 DE genes at FDR<0.05. A volcano plot was generated. Enrichment analysis was omitted due to library availability but the gene set and method were defined. Overall, the implementation follows the revised plan and tests the hypothesis.

PREVIOUS EXPLORATION:

Hypothesis: Patient age at diagnosis is inversely correlated with expression of a proliferation gene signature (e.g., MKI67, PCNA, MCM family).

Experiment objective: Compute a proliferation score per sample and test its correlation with age.

Steps for the programmer:
1. Define a proliferation signature gene list: MKI67, PCNA, MCM2–MCM7.  
2. Map each symbol to its Ensembl ID via mygene and extract expression rows.  
3. For each sample, compute the mean expression across these genes as the proliferation score.  
4. Merge proliferation scores with age_at_diagnosis.  
5. Plot scatter of proliferation score vs age; compute Spearman correlation and p‐value.  
6. Divide patients into age quartiles and compare proliferation score across quartiles via Kruskal–Wallis test.

Deliverables:
• Proliferation score per sample.  
• Scatter plot with Spearman ρ and p‐value.  
• Kruskal–Wallis statistic and p‐value across age quartiles.  
• Boxplot of proliferation score by age quartile.

Analysis:
The proliferation score was successfully computed for 462 patients (mean ≈5.03, SD ≈0.60). Spearman correlation between age at diagnosis and proliferation score was effectively zero (ρ=–0.002, p=0.966), indicating no monotonic relationship. Comparing proliferation scores across age quartiles via Kruskal–Wallis yielded H=7.134 (p=0.0678), also non‐significant. Overall, there is no evidence that proliferation signature expression is inversely correlated with age in this cohort.

Review:
Hypothesis: Patient age at diagnosis is inversely correlated with expression of a proliferation gene signature (MKI67, PCNA, MCM2–MCM7).

Implementation followed the plan: proliferative gene symbols were mapped to Ensembl IDs, expression values were extracted, and a proliferation score (mean expression) was computed for each of 462 samples with available age data. Spearman correlation between age_at_diagnosis and proliferation score was effectively zero (rho = –0.002, p = 0.966), indicating no monotonic relationship. When dividing patients into age quartiles, the Kruskal–Wallis test yielded H = 7.134 (p = 0.0678), also non‐significant.

Conclusion: There is no evidence supporting an inverse correlation between patient age and the proliferation signature in this cohort.

Hypothesis: Patients who received systemic therapy prior to sample collection have higher tumor mutational burden and distinct variant classification profiles compared to therapy‐naïve patients.

Experiment objective: Compare mutational burden and mutation type distributions between patients with and without prior systemic therapy.

Steps for the programmer:
1. Load cleaned_clinical_data.csv and cleaned_mutations.csv.
2. From clinical data, select patients with prior_systemic_therapy labeled YES or NO.
3. From mutations data, count total somatic mutations per patient to define TMB.
4. Merge TMB counts with therapy indicator for each patient.
5. Compare TMB between therapy vs no‐therapy groups using a Wilcoxon rank‐sum test.
6. For each patient, compute the proportion of each Variant_Classification (e.g., Missense_Mutation, Nonsense_Mutation, Silent).
7. Aggregate proportions by therapy group and compare distributions using chi‐square tests or logistic regression per classification category.
8. Visualize: (a) boxplot of TMB by therapy group, (b) stacked bar plot of average mutation type proportions in each group.

Deliverables:
• Table of median TMB, Wilcoxon statistic, and p‐value.
• Mutation type proportion table by therapy group and chi‐square test p‐values.
• Boxplot of TMB by prior systemic therapy status.
• Stacked bar plot of variant classification proportions.
• Interpretive summary on how prior therapy associates with mutational patterns.

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu, chi2_contingency

# 1. Load data
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv', low_memory=False)
mutations = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv', low_memory=False)

# 2. Prepare therapy indicator
clin_ther = clinical[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'prior_systemic_therapy']].rename(
    columns={'bcr_patient_barcode': 'patient_id'}
)
clin_ther = clin_ther[clin_ther['prior_systemic_therapy'].isin(['YES', 'NO'])]

# 3. Compute TMB: total mutations per patient, include zeros
tmb_counts = mutations['patient_id'].value_counts().rename_axis('patient_id').reset_index(name='tmb')
tmb_df = clin_ther.merge(tmb_counts, on='patient_id', how='left')
tmb_df['tmb'] = tmb_df['tmb'].fillna(0).astype(int)

# 4. Compare TMB between therapy groups
grouped = tmb_df.groupby('prior_systemic_therapy')['tmb']
median_tmb = grouped.median()
counts_group = tmb_df['prior_systemic_therapy'].value_counts()
yes_tmb = tmb_df.loc[tmb_df['prior_systemic_therapy']=='YES', 'tmb']
no_tmb  = tmb_df.loc[tmb_df['prior_systemic_therapy']=='NO',  'tmb']
stat, p_val = mannwhitneyu(yes_tmb, no_tmb, alternative='two-sided')

print("Patient counts by therapy group:")
print(counts_group.to_string(), "\n")
print("Median TMB by group:")
print(median_tmb.to_string(), "\n")
print(f"Wilcoxon rank-sum test: statistic = {stat:.2f}, p-value = {p_val:.4g}\n")

# 5. Compute Variant Classification proportions per patient

{"code":"import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns
from scipy.stats import mannwhitneyu, chi2_contingency

# 1. Load data
clinical = pd.read_csv('cleaned_clinical_data.csv', low_memory=False)
mutations = pd.read_csv('cleaned_mutations.csv', low_memory=False)

# 2. Prepare therapy indicator
clin_ther = clinical[['bcr_patient_barcode', 'prior_systemic_therapy']].rename(
    columns={'bcr_patient_barcode': 'patient_id'}
)
clin_ther = clin_ther[clin_ther['prior_systemic_therapy'].isin(['YES', 'NO'])]

# 3. Compute TMB: total mutations per patient
tmb_counts = mutations['patient_id'].value_counts().rename_axis('patient_id').reset_index(name='tmb')
tmb_df = clin_ther.merge(tmb_counts, on='patient_id', how='left')
tmb_df['tmb'] = tmb_df['tmb'].fillna(0).astype(int)

# 4. Compare TMB between therapy groups
counts_group = tmb_df['prior_systemic_therapy'].value_counts()
yes_tmb = tmb_df.loc[tmb_df['prior_systemic_therapy']=='YES', 'tmb']
no_tmb  = tmb_df.loc[tmb_df['prior_systemic_therapy']=='NO',  'tmb']
stat, p_val = mannwhitneyu(yes_tmb, no_tmb, alternative='two-sided')

print("Patient counts by therapy group:")
print(counts_group.to_string(), "\n")
print("Median TMB by group:")
print(tmb_df.groupby('prior_systemic_therapy')['tmb'].median().to_string(), "\n")
print(f"Wilcoxon rank-sum test: statistic = {stat:.2f}, p-value = {p_val:.4g}\n")

# 5. Compute Variant Classification proportions per patient
vc_counts = mutations.groupby(['patient_id', 'Variant_Classification']).size().unstack(fill_value=0)
vc_props = vc_counts.div(vc_counts.sum(axis=1), axis=0).reset_index()
vc_props = vc_props.merge(clin_ther, on='patient_id', how='inner')
# average proportions per therapy group (select only classification columns)
class_cols = vc_counts.columns.tolist()
mean_props = vc_props.groupby('prior_systemic_therapy')[class_cols].mean().T

# 6. Chi-square test on aggregated counts
agg = mutations.merge(clin_ther, on='patient_id', how='inner')
cont_table = pd.crosstab(agg['prior_systemic_therapy'], agg['Variant_Classification'])
chi2, chi_p, dof, ex = chi2_contingency(cont_table)

print("Chi-square test on variant classification distributions:")
print(f"chi2 = {chi2:.2f}, p-value = {chi_p:.4g}, dof = {dof}\n")
print("Average variant classification proportions by group:")
print(mean_props, "\n")

# 7a. Visualization: TMB boxplot
plt.figure(figsize=(6, 4))
sns.boxplot(x='prior_systemic_therapy', y='tmb', data=tmb_df, palette='Set2')
plt.title('Tumor Mutational Burden by Prior Systemic Therapy')
plt.xlabel('Prior Systemic Therapy')
plt.ylabel('TMB (mutation count)')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

# 7b. Visualization: stacked bar plot of mean proportions
mean_props.plot(kind='bar', stacked=True, figsize=(8, 5), colormap='tab20')
plt.title('Mean Variant Classification Proportions by Therapy Group')
plt.xlabel('Variant Classification')
plt.ylabel('Proportion')
plt.legend(title='Therapy Group', labels=mean_props.columns.tolist(), bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left')
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()"}
